value.deck: Azure App Service has entered public preview for Markdown rendering support, enabling agent-based applications to serve formatted content directly.
shortVersion: Microsoft has announced a public preview for Markdown rendering support targeting agent-based applications on Azure App Service. The release notes establish that this feature simplifies how hosted AI services serve formatted content, though specific rendering mechanisms remain unspecified.

The reporting confirms richer structured output handling for App Service-hosted agents, but only implies streamlined integration with client interfaces. Developers should evaluate potential rendering security risks and output validation pipelines as this preview evolves.
value.plainLanguage: Azure App Service now includes a public preview feature for rendering Markdown to streamline formatted output from hosted AI agents.

keyTerms.meaning: Platform-level capability in Azure App Service to process and format structured text generated by hosted AI agents.
Software architectures hosted on Azure where AI agents generate responses and execute tasks.

value.whyItMatters: Native Markdown support simplifies rich text delivery for hosted agents, though architectural implications regarding payload parsing and output sanitization require validation during preview testing.
watchNext: Track updates to Azure App Service documentation for explicit security guidelines on sanitizing agent-rendered Markdown.
Observe transition timelines from public preview to general availability for production deployment commitments.
